name: Standoff Height Planner
blurb: standoff length from the tallest part under the board
intro: The shortest standoff that keeps the tallest bottom-side part (or through-hole lead) clear of the floor, rounded up to a stock length; or, for two stacked boards, the spacing their parts and board-to-board connector need. A screw length for a female-threaded standoff comes with it. Gaps and thread engagement are rules of thumb stated in the notes.

inputs.label: Through-hole lead protrusion
inputs.help: IPC-A-610: 2.5 mm at most; 0 for SMT-only boards.

inputs.label: Floor boss height
inputs.help: If the standoff sits on a raised boss, its height counts.

inputs.label: The tall parts may sit over each other
inputs.help: Off when you know they are apart in x/y: then only the taller one counts.

inputs.label: Tolerance allowance
inputs.help: Standoff and part height tolerances together.

examples.title: Board with a 3 mm SMD inductor and THT leads underneath
Two boards joined by an 11 mm mezzanine connector

usage: Mode floor: give the tallest bottom part and lead protrusion, the boss height and tallest top part; mode stack: the lower board's tallest top part, the upper board's tallest bottom part, whether they may overlap, and the board-to-board connector mated height if any. All in mm, plus the air gap, tolerance, board thickness and screw size. It returns the minimum and stock standoff length, the air gap it leaves, board and part heights above the floor, and a screw length for a female standoff. Use it when choosing spacers or the enclosure height.
sources: IPC-6012 bow and twist 0.75 % for SMT boards
Thread engagement ≥ 1.5·d for a steel screw in a softer internal thread: Machinery's Handbook / VDI 2230 rule of thumb
Stock standoff lengths: Würth WA-SSTII, Keystone and Ettinger catalogues; screw lengths ISO 7045 / ISO 4762
